title: Write design/daw-sidecars.md §Formats and the go/no-go on writing .asd
description:
## Intent
Turn the spike's findings into the design note every later milestone cites, and put the go/no-go to the owner.

## Scope
- New `design/daw-sidecars.md`, section **§Formats**: `.asd` table (fields, encoding, versions), `.alc` minimal document, how each ties to its audio, beat numbering (negative beats, before-first/after-last behaviour), detune range, warp-mode table.
- Section **§Decision**: go / no-go on writing `.asd`, and what M2 writes in each case.
- Section **§Open**: anything unknown, with the evidence.
- A Mermaid diagram of the round trip (Apricity manifest → sidecar → the DAW → edited sidecar → import).

## Out of scope
The Apricity mapping and naming rules (M1 adds §Mapping, M3 §Naming).

## Verify
a case-insensitive grep of `design/daw-sidecars.md` for the DAW's brand and product names finds nothing; the owner's sign-off comment is on the M0 epic.

Commit: `chore(<this id>): design note for DAW sidecar formats`.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
